expectations.text: The artifact is routed to Feature Design Doc from semantic intent and passes the bundled validator in strict mode with the full profile.
expectations.evidence: The artifact frontmatter declares doc-type: Feature Design Doc and profile: full. The deterministic grading record reports validate_fdd.py --strict return_code 0, profile full, passed true, major_count 0, and no findings.

expectations.text: All required numbered sections and six cross-cutting concerns are present.
expectations.evidence: saved-search-filters.md contains numbered sections 1 through 13, including the required feature-definition, flow, design, policy, alternatives, scope, and risks sections. Section 11 contains Security, Privacy, Permissions, Observability, Accessibility, and Internationalization.

expectations.text: Ownership, 20-item limit, case-insensitive uniqueness, server-side JSON persistence, and partial application have clear canonical owning sections.
expectations.evidence: The canonical policy rules appear in section 9: Ownership and Visibility, Name Uniqueness, Capacity, Degradation, and Persistence and Data Minimization. These sections explicitly state owner-only visibility, a maximum of 20 per user-workspace pair, case-insensitive uniqueness, server JSON persistence, and valid-only partial application with notice.

expectations.text: Flows, Scope, Cross-cutting Concerns, and Result Semantics project only their responsibility instead of fully restating exact policy rules and rationale.
expectations.evidence: The flows describe user-visible save, apply, rename, delete, failure, and partial-success sequences; Scope lists v1.0 inclusions and exclusions; Cross-cutting Concerns addresses security, privacy, permissions, observability, accessibility, and internationalization. The design and failure sections reference the policies as needed without turning each area into a duplicate policy rationale.

expectations.text: The v1.0 exclusions and both evidence-backed rejected alternatives appear in the correct responsibilities.
expectations.evidence: Section 12 excludes shared filters, default filters, custom sorting, and localStorage for v1.0. Section 10 records localStorage as rejected because it does not support multi-device use, and workspace-shared filters as rejected because permissions and ownership become complex and exceed the v1.0 personal-filter scope.

expectations.text: The document contains no implementation task sequence, source file path, function name, or PR breakdown.
expectations.evidence: The document explicitly states it is not an implementation task list, file/function guide, work sequence, or test plan. Its content remains feature decisions, policies, flows, scope, risks, and open questions; no source paths, function names, or PR breakdown are present.

claims.claim: The generated artifact passes strict full-profile FDD structural validation.
claims.evidence: deterministic-grading.json records validate_fdd.py --strict with return_code 0, passed true, profile full, and zero findings.

claims.claim: The artifact preserves the supplied product decisions without adding implementation scope.
claims.evidence: The document covers the supplied ownership, persistence, capacity, uniqueness, partial-application, security, privacy, accessibility, internationalization, observability, exclusions, and rejected alternatives, while explicitly disclaiming implementation actions.

uncertainties: The document leaves name length and whitespace rules, observability retention, and condition/search-value size as NEEDS INPUT items, consistent with information not supplied by the prompt.

eval_feedback.overall: All six task-specific expectations are satisfied; the artifact is structurally valid and keeps policy ownership and scope boundaries clear.
